# zerobas roadmap

zerobas is a **clean-room reimplementation of MSX1 system software** — three
components (BASIC interpreter + cassette + disk) combined with an open BIOS (C-BIOS)
only at runtime — with **two co-equal goals**: the clean-room implementations
themselves, and the clean-provenance **documentation** of how these systems work
that the same discipline yields (see [`MISSION.md`](MISSION.md)). Scope today
is MSX1; the BASIC half targets **faithful, full MSX1 BASIC** (Phase 1 shipped the
*game-loader-stub* subset — enough to boot disk/tape game loaders — and the charter
has since been raised to full-language faithfulness, pursued in Phase 3), while tape
and disk are device-complete (read **and** write).

See [`README.md`](README.md) for the charter and the legal/provenance firewall,
[`PROVENANCE.md`](PROVENANCE.md) for the traceability rules every item below must
honour (allowed sources only; no disassembly), and
[`docs/dev-workflow.md`](docs/dev-workflow.md) for how to implement + validate one
item — do **one item per session** to keep context lean.

## Phases at a glance

| Phase | Scope | State |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — loader-stub BASIC + transports + standardization** | just enough MSX-BASIC to run `.BAS`/binary loader stubs; tape + disk read/write; standard DSKIO/`HPHYD` interfaces | **✅ closed** |
| **2 — full disk (Disk BASIC integration)** | the full file-channel verb surface (sequential + random-access + dir mgmt + `CALL FORMAT`), all oracle-validated | **✅ verb surface complete** — only the Tier-2 provider oracle (a distinct DOS-boot sub-track) + a few Phase-3-gated verbs remain |
| **3+ — full MSX1 BASIC** | floating point, full string engine, arrays, graphics, sound, … | **active charter** (raised from loader-stub) — landed: string engine, float pack, math pack, **arrays/DIM arc CONCLUDED** (through slice-4c string-scalar unification — the faithful unified variable area; no fixed variable pool remains) |

- [x] 🔴 **`PRINT USING "**$##.##"` PUTS THE `$` AT THE FIELD'S LEFT EDGE; THE VG-8020
      FLOATS IT AGAINST THE DIGITS (D-PUSTARDOL, found 2026-10-29 by the program
      ladder's ledger).**
      🎚️ TIER 1 — a common money format prints `$***5.00` where the reference prints
      `***$5.00`; twelve shapes measured, ALL differ the same way
      ([`pustardol_measure.out`](scratchpad/pustardol_measure.out)): the `$` sits
      right before the digits AFTER any sign (`**-$5.00`, `+**$` -> `***+$5.00`),
      `**$.##` floats too (`*$0.50`), overflow is `%$123456.00`.
      🤖 **AUTONOMOUS** — but it needs ROOM FIRST.
      ➡️ **The change is known (~22 B):** in basic/pu-render.inc `ptf_star`, after
      the `**` pair, a `$` followed by `#` or `.` sets PU_TYPE bit2 (the floating
      `$` the emitter already handles for `$$`) plus a NEW bit3 "single dollar",
      and is consumed; `ptf_num_fill` adds 1 column, not 2, when bit3 is set
      (PU_TYPE's readers all mask `and $03` / `and $04`, and the per-field reset
      clears the byte); `ptf_plus` accepts `*` after the `+` as it accepts `#`
      and `$`.
      🔴 **THE WALL:** the scanner is included ONLY in sub page 0 (sub/printusing.asm),
      which had **1 B free** on 2026-10-29, and a page-0 tenant cannot reach sub
      page 1. Carve options, unpriced: an instruction-pair factoring of sub page 0
      (the main-ROM pair scan once found 113 B), or move a small page-0 tenant
      (keystr_tenant, ~284 B incl. its 160-B image) to sub2 -- which needs a sub2
      inline call stub in main, and main's low region had 1 B free on 2026-10-29.
      The ledger avoids `**$` meanwhile (L3_ledger.bas line 350).
      📏 **Route D measured 2026-10-29 for this wall: shut.** jp -> jr over the cold
      page-0 files (sub/deffn.asm 18 sites, sub/tkfloat.asm 10, sub/keystr.asm 1,
      sub/printusing.asm 1): 1 of 30 in range, worth 1 B (built, reverted). The hot
      ones (graphics, strheap, arrays) were left out on purpose -- a taken `jr` costs
      2 T more. The next try is the instruction-pair factoring or the tenant move.
      ✅ **FIXED 2026-10-29, AFTER TWO CARVES IN sub/strheap.asm** (sub page 0:
      1 -> 32 -> 60 B free before the fix, 16 B after it): the instruction-pair
      factoring did it. `ld (iy+SHB_ERR),a / ret` stood at 27 sites -> one shared
      tail `she_seterr_ret` (8 sites reach it with `jr`, 19 with `jp`: +31 B);
      `ld l,(ix+12) / ld h,(ix+13)` (8 sites) and its store (6) -> `she_ldhl_ix12`
      / `she_sthl_ix12` (+28 B). Pairs were counted only when strictly adjacent
      (no label between), so no jump lands inside one. Then the change as planned,
      including `**$.##` and `+**$`: 12 of 12 shapes now match
      ([`pustardol_after.out`](scratchpad/pustardol_after.out)). Gate
      pustardol-acceptance (both targets against the VG-8020: the CF-3300 lacks
      the floating dollar), knife K-D ([`pustardol_knife.out`](scratchpad/pustardol_knife.out)).
      The ledger uses `**$` again.
      🔁 **THE CARVE COST SPEED, AND THE LADDER CAUGHT IT.** `she_ldhl_ix12` /
      `she_sthl_ix12` sat in the garbage collector's per-element loops (the sweep,
      the array walk, the shellsort): L3_report ran 0.4 s slower and gained a late
      interrupt. Those loops now keep the pointer in HL or on the stack (neither
      sg_move_one nor sg_visit touches ix+12..15), which is FASTER than before the
      carve and gave 14 B more: sub page 0 has 24 B free after D-LATEINT's 6.

- [x] 🔴 **`USR(S$)` WAS TYPE MISMATCH; THE VG-8020 HANDS THE ROUTINE THE STRING'S
      DESCRIPTOR (D-USRSTR, found 2026-10-29 by the program ladder's L4_machine).**
      🎚️ TIER 1 — passing a string to machine code is ordinary USR use.
      🤖 **AUTONOMOUS.** Measured ([`usrstr_measure.out`](scratchpad/usrstr_measure.out)):
      DAC+2 = the [len][ptr] descriptor, for a variable its OWN one
      (`USR(S$)=VARPTR(S$)`), VALTYP 3; temporaries live during the call; a
      routine that leaves VALTYP 3 in a numeric place is 13.
      ✅ **FIXED 2026-10-29.** basic/usr.asm `ev_usr` probes the argument with
      `str_eval` from a saved IX: a string that is the WHOLE argument goes in as
      above, anything else (`USR("A"="A")`, a number) the numeric way from the
      same start. `usr_ret` answers VALTYP 3 with the deferred 13. Main page 1,
      from a pin pad. Gate usrstr-acceptance (9 rows), knife K-U
      ([`usrstr_knife.out`](scratchpad/usrstr_knife.out)). The ladder runner's
      prompt normaliser now also takes `ZB` drawn over a line the program filled.

- [ ] 🔴 **A USR ROUTINE CANNOT RETURN A STRING (D-USRSTRRES, found 2026-10-29 with
      D-USRSTR).**
      🎚️ TIER 1 — on the VG-8020 a routine that leaves VALTYP 3 makes USR a
      string: `PRINT USR1("ABC")` prints `ABC`, `B$=USR1(S$)` is `HELLO`
      ([`usrstr_measure.out`](scratchpad/usrstr_measure.out) rows C / D); zerobas
      says 13.
      🤖 **AUTONOMOUS** — but it is architecture. USR's type is known only after the
      routine runs, and zerobas evaluates strings and numbers in two parsers that
      PROBE (`str_eval` declines, the numeric parse starts again from the same
      cursor). A string-context USR must run the routine inside `str_eval`; when
      the routine then returns a NUMBER (`PRINT USR(5)`), the numeric re-parse
      must not run it a second time (catusr-acceptance pins "exactly once"). A
      one-shot cache keyed on the cursor -- the result and the cursor after it --
      is the cheapest shape found; price it before building.

- [x] 🔴 **`PRINT USING` PRINTED A TINY NUMBER'S DIGITS AS IF IT WERE NOT TINY
      (D-PUTINY, found 2026-10-29 by the program ladder's L4_tables).**
      🎚️ TIER 1 — a trig table printed COS(90°) as `-3.38082` where the VG-8020
      prints `-0.00000`: any value that PRINT writes in E form (` 3.38081E-15 `)
      reached the fixed renderer, whose walk read digits, a point and digits and
      stopped at the `E` (also `F #.#`;1D-20 gave `1.1`). A LARGE one did the
      same: `#######`;1D+15 gave `      2`.
      🤖 **AUTONOMOUS.** Measured on the VG-8020
      ([`putiny_measure.out`](scratchpad/putiny_measure.out),
      [`putiny_big.out`](scratchpad/putiny_big.out),
      [`putiny_neg.out`](scratchpad/putiny_neg.out),
      [`putiny_wide.out`](scratchpad/putiny_wide.out)): a small value rounds
      half-up into the places like any other (`5D-6` -> `+0.00001`, `4D-6` ->
      `+0.00000`); a large one is `%`, a space and PRINT's own E text, in ANY
      field: unpadded, its `-` dropped, `+` / trailing `-` / `**` / `$$` ignored.
      ✅ **FIXED 2026-10-29.** sub/punum.asm `pnt_norm` (sub page 1) rewrites
      flt_fmt's `E-nn` text as `.000ddd` (n-1 zeros, at most 28 digits) before the
      walk, and turns `E+nn` into the finished `% ` + text; the sign and emit
      tenants pass a PU_NUM that starts with `%` through untouched (sub page 0,
      12 B). Gate putiny-acceptance, knives K-T / K-B
      ([`putiny_knife.out`](scratchpad/putiny_knife.out)).

- [x] 🔴 **A NEGATIVE FRACTION WITH NO ROOM FOR `-0` OVERFLOWS; THE VG-8020 DROPS THE
      ZERO (D-PUNEGLEAD, found 2026-10-29 measuring D-PUTINY).**
      🎚️ TIER 1 — `PRINT USING "#.##";-.5` is `-.50` on the VG-8020 and `%-0.50`
      here; `#.#`;-.04 is `-.0` / `%-0.0`; with room (`##.#`) both print `-0.5`
      ([`putiny_lead.out`](scratchpad/putiny_lead.out)). Also `+.#`;-.5 is `-.5`
      there and `+%-.5` here: the scanner takes `+.` apart.
      🤖 **AUTONOMOUS.** Measured 2026-10-29 with `**`, `$$`, commas, `^^^^`
      and the sign forms ([`puneglead_measure.out`](scratchpad/puneglead_measure.out),
      [`puneglead_both.out`](scratchpad/puneglead_both.out)).
      ✅ **FIXED 2026-10-29: ONE RULE AND TWO SCANNER GAPS.**
      - A lone `0.` loses its `0` when the FINISHED field would not fit -- a
        positive value's coming `+` counts too (`+.##`;.5 is `+.50`), a real
        integer digit still overflows (-.996 is `%-1.00`). sub/punum.asm
        `pnt_term`, sub page 1.
      - `+.##` and `$$.##` are fields: basic/pu-render.inc `ptf_plus` /
        `ptf_dollar` accept a `.`; `$$` keeps its integer column (`$0.50`,
        punum's `pnt_intdone`).
      - After a LEADING sign, a trailing `+` / `-` is a literal (`+.##+`;-.25
        is `-.25+`); it used to replace the leading sign, which was wrong
        before today too (`+#.##-`;.25 gave `0.25+`). The two trailing-sign
        arms now share one body, which paid for the test: sub page 0 went
        4 -> 14 B.
      Gate puneglead-acceptance (11 rows), knives K-Z / K-S / K-L / K-D
      ([`puneglead_knife.out`](scratchpad/puneglead_knife.out)).

- [x] 🔬 **`COS(4*ATN(1#)/2)` IS `-6.2831853071796E-14` ON THE VG-8020 AND
      `-3.3808E-15` HERE (D-COSHALFPI, found 2026-10-29 measuring D-PUTINY).**
      🎚️ TIER 1 — a printed number differs in a plain calculation (as D-POWNEG).
      Both are rounding noise around 0, but they are not the same noise, and
      zerobas's prints only 5 significant digits of a double
      ([`putiny_measure.out`](scratchpad/putiny_measure.out) row G).
      🤖 **AUTONOMOUS** — measure COS / SIN / TAN near their zeros, single and
      double, before touching the math pack.
      ✅ **MEASURED 2026-10-29 — INSIDE THE RULED CLASS, NOTHING TO CHANGE IN THE
      ROM** ([`coshalfpi_measure.out`](scratchpad/coshalfpi_measure.out)). Near
      their zeros the VG-8020's SIN / COS / TAN come in whole steps of
      2π·1E-14 (COS(π/2) -1 step, SIN(π) -2, COS(1.5707963267948) +1, also in
      single precision): it reduces the angle as x·(1/2π) in 14 digits and
      keeps the fraction, and its cosine is a quarter turn added in those units
      (a Python model of that reduction matches SIN(100), SIN(π/6), COS(π) to
      1E-12 -- scratchpad session model, not kept). zerobas's `-3.3808E-15` IS
      the true value to its digits (cos(1.5707963267949) = -3.38076868E-15);
      it prints 5 digits because the angle itself carries no more. Joost's
      2026-07-13 ruling (COS.md / SIN.md, Differences 1) keeps the accurate
      answer. 🔴 MY FILING'S "zerobas's prints only 5 significant digits of a
      double" read as a defect; it is the information the 14-digit angle holds.

      fractional 30/32. BOTH machines compute `x^-n` as `1/(x^n)` (320/320 each),
      so every negative-power difference is the reference's DIVISION landing low

      (docs/concepts/numbers.md). The fractional ones are the EXP / LOG class,
      also ruled (docs/keywords/EXP.md). Against exact arithmetic zerobas is the
      closer in 182 of 191; the 8 the other way are truncation luck on an
      already-rounded operand, the visible one `.5^-23`: 8388608 there,
      8388608.0000001 here (true reciprocal of the 14-digit `.5^23`:
      8388608.000000088). 🔴 THE DOC WAS WRONG: numbers.md said the division
      difference needs a divisor of more than 10 digits; `1/1.00625` (6 digits)
      differs too. Corrected.

- [ ] 🔴 **STUDY: DEFERRED ERRORS VS RAISING AT THE POINT OF DETECTION — HOW MUCH OF
      THE PER-COMMAND "WHICH ERROR WINS" CODE EXISTS ONLY BECAUSE ZEROBAS DEFERS?
      (D-DEFERRSTUDY, filed 2026-10-24 at Joost's request.)**
      🎚️ TIER 1 — ruled by Joost 2026-10-24: *"it doesn't really fit the tiers I
      guess, so just file as tier 1"*. It is an architecture question, not a keyword.
      🤖 **AUTONOMOUS** — the study (inventory, one prototype family, the
      numbers). The decision to convert beyond that family goes back to Joost
      with the numbers, at step 3 below: it changes the error architecture.
      📏 **Why it was raised.** Joost, on D-CLEAR3ARG: *"every fix like that makes
      me worry we're introducing a ton of command specific error handling, while
      reference probably has generic mechanisms mostly?"* Black-box, the VG-8020
      behaves as if each fault is raised the moment it is detected, so precedence
      falls out of parse order: D-CLEAR3ARG (overflow, then statement end, then the
      range checks) and D-ERRORARG (expression fault, then byte range, then end,
      then 0) both measured exactly that. zerobas instead records many faults as
      PENDING (`penderr_set`, first-error-wins) and raises them at
      `check_expr_errors`, so each site has to rebuild the reference's order by hand
      (D-CLEAR3ARG needed an `fperr_test` arm plus an end check routed through the
      pending path to keep the POOLSIZE restore). At filing: 19 `penderr_set` call
      sites, 17 `check_expr_errors` sites, 9 `stmt_bare_end` callers.
      🎯 **The deferral looks historical.** D-F2-1's deferred discipline predates
      `raise_error`, and [`spec-basic-error-handling.md`](docs/spec-basic-error-handling.md)
      itself says the `SAVSTK` reset lets an error from ANY depth unwind cleanly,
      "strictly more robust", anticipating "a future non-deferred site". So an
      immediate raise from inside an expression is mechanically possible TODAY.
      ⚠️ **What is NOT known, and must be measured, not assumed:** which deferred
      sites protect state an immediate raise would leave half-written — D-CLEARFIT's
      POOLSIZE restore is one; DEF FN shadow frames, string temporaries, a
      half-assigned variable (`var_store_fac`'s contract), FIELD / file state are
      candidates.
      ➡️ **Plan.**
      1. Inventory every deferred-error writer and every realisation point; for
         each, classify "an immediate raise is equivalent" vs "it protects state
         (name the state)". A table in a spec, with file:line.
      2. Prototype ONE family on a branch — the argument range checks are the
         likeliest (the `get_int16_checked` / `eval_byte_checked` callers) — as an
         immediate raise; run the FULL battery, the TIER 6 error rows, the tape
         collection; price the bytes (expected to go DOWN: ordering code deleted).
      3. Report to Joost: bytes, rows moved, what state-protecting sites remain,
         and whether new "which error wins" items would become deletions rather than
         additions. He decides whether to convert further.
      🔴 **Until then, every TIER 6 fix prefers an existing generic path** (as
      D-USRBARE, D-CONTPROG and D-ERRORARG did) and says so in its ✅ note when it
      had to add a site-specific check instead.

      operand reads **0 on the VG-8020 and 1 here** for `1/0`, `(1/0)*`, `SQR(-1)` and
      `ASC("")` -- four observable divergences caused by deferral alone, so the

- [x] 🧱 **D-FLDDESC — FIELD AS THE REFERENCE DOES IT: NO TABLE, THE VARIABLE'S OWN
      DESCRIPTOR POINTS INTO THE CHANNEL'S RECORD AT BLOCK+9 (filed 2026-10-17)** —
      ✅ **BUILT 2026-10-17: main page 1 168 -> 379 B free, sub page 0 29 -> 177 B,
      sub page 1 1104 -> 1165 B, disk.rom 2857 -> 2865 B (`make basic-reloc`).**
      🎚️ BUDGET — main page 1 (D-ROMSIZE step 1) — and TIER 5 (every string-variable
      read on a disk machine stops paying fld_lookup).
      🤖 **AUTONOMOUS** — 🏗️ Joost 2026-10-17: disk.rom owns the FIELD table (diskless
      it is ERR 5), and *"if reference has a location inside the non-disk region it
      uses, we should also use that"*.
      📏 **MEASURED FIRST** ([`fieldram_probe.py`](scratchpad/fieldram_probe.py) ->
      [`fieldram_run.out`](scratchpad/fieldram_run.out); BASIC VARPTR / PEEK / FRE
      only; VARPTR is signed, so the readings show +65536): after
      `FIELD #1,2 AS A$,3 AS B$` on the CF-3300, A$'s descriptor is [2][VARPTR(#1)+9]
      and B$'s [3][VARPTR(#1)+11]; FIELD spends 0 B of FRE(0) and FRE(""); LSET keeps
      the pointer and writes the bytes there; a plain `A$="Z"` moves it to string
      space. So the reference keeps NO table: the location is the variable itself
      plus the channel's record buffer. zerobas leaves the descriptor empty (length
      0) and keeps FLD_TAB. 🔮 "0 B, into the channel block, 2 B apart": HIT.
      🧭 **DESIGN (nothing in the way, checked 2026-10-17):** the string GC already
      skips a descriptor whose pointer is outside the heap (sub/strheap.asm
      `sg_inrange`; D-LITREF's program-text pointers live with it), and a
      non-FIELDed LSET / RSET already writes in place into the target's own body at
      its own length (docs/spec-basic-lrvar.md) -- which IS a fielded store once the
      descriptor points at the record. So: FIELD writes [w][block+9+offset] into each
      variable; LSET / RSET keep only their non-FIELDed arm; fld_lookup leaves
      str_eval's variable path; FLD_TAB, FLD_DESC, fld_find / fld_add / fld_init and
      the sub FLDLOOK tenant go. ⛓️ PREREQUISITE: RANDOM's record must live at
      block+9 (today it travels through FSECTOR_BUF via t_fch_load / t_fch_save:
      S10.E's next item), so GET / PUT and FIELD agree on one buffer.
      ⚠️ Also seen: the channel block sits 265 B below HIMEM on the CF-3300 and 665 B
      on zerobas (MAXFILES=1) -- a TIER-4 RAM reading for the FCH block layout, not
      this item's.
      📏 **ROUND 2, THE ROWS THE TWO MODELS READ DIFFERENTLY** ([`flddesc_probe.py`](scratchpad/flddesc_probe.py)
      -> [`flddesc_run.out`](scratchpad/flddesc_run.out), LEN=8, A$ 2 B and B$ 3 B
      fielded): the CF-3300 reads r1 `XY  Z` (LSET / RSET), r2 `QY` (MID$ writes the
      record), r3 `XY` (GET re-reads it), r4 `XYMN` (a copy taken before LSET is its
      own), r5 `XYMN` and r6 `XYXY` (SWAP exchanges the DESCRIPTORS: C$ is fielded
      after it), r7 `  Z` (the buffer survives CLOSE), r8 `  Z` (and a re-OPEN does NOT
      clear it), r9 `  Z`. 🔮 r1-r7 and r9 as predicted: HIT; r8 was unpredicted.
      🔴 **zerobas stops at r2 with `Illegal function call in 60`**: MID$ on a fielded
      variable finds its own (empty) descriptor -- a real divergence today, and the
      descriptor model removes it by construction. These nine rows are the slice's
      gate. ⚠️ r8 also says hk_frnd's space-fill of the record at OPEN is not the
      reference's on a RE-open; what a FRESH block holds is unmeasured.
      📏 **ROUND 3, A FRESH BLOCK** (`FLDDESC_PROG=fresh` ->
      [`fldfresh_run.out`](scratchpad/fldfresh_run.out)): the CF-3300 NEVER fills the
      record -- #1 reads 159 146 and #2 255 255 right after MAXFILES (leftover RAM),
      and after CLEAR + MAXFILES an old `QQ` is still there (81 81). 🔮 "spaces": MISS.
      So hk_frnd's OPEN fill went too; f1 / f2 are leftover RAM on both machines and
      not comparable, f3 is.
      ✅ **THE SLICE.** Drafted by a subagent in its own worktree (build + unit tests
      only), integrated and measured here:
      - RANDOM's record LIVES at block+9: disk.rom's frnd_calc / GET's end fill use
        `rnd_rec` (the row's cached block); sub's t_fch_load keeps only the LOF / LOC
        mirror, t_fch_save is gone (row 21 is `fp_stash_ok`, rows keep their numbers).
      - FIELD writes `[w][block+9+offset]` into the target (scalar or element,
        `tgt_store_desc`), ERR 50 checked first; FLD_TAB, FLD_DESC, fld_find / fld_add
        / fld_init / fld_init_g / fld_clear_chan / fld_lookup, the sub page-0 FLDLOOK
        tenant (row 12 retired) and ERASE's aer_fldfix are gone; a string-variable
        read no longer consults any table.
      - LSET / RSET keep only the in-place arm; hk_lrset is its three call-backs.
      - hk_frnd no longer blanks the record (round 3).
      - Pins: the freed bytes ahead of $6CF3 / $72D4 / $73AC were refilled exactly by
        moved code (lrset_finish / lrset_store, GET / PUT's head, ex_delete, exf_comma,
        derive_directf, dir_line / run_kw, relink, trace_line); 6/6, waste 4 of 4;
        `make switch-build-check` 7/7.
      Witness: [`flddesc_run_after.out`](scratchpad/flddesc_run_after.out) r1-r9 SAME
      on both machines (r2 was `Illegal function call`);
      [`fieldram_run_after.out`](scratchpad/fieldram_run_after.out) [a] / [b] / [l]
      byte-identical offsets and lengths; [`fldfresh_run_after.out`](scratchpad/fldfresh_run_after.out)
      f3 SAME. 🔮 "r1-r7 + r9 match, r8 differs while the fill stays": HIT; after
      the fill went, r8 SAME. Knife connectedness unchanged: HIT.
      🏗️ **Joost 2026-10-17 reversed his 2026-09-27 "keep ours"** on a fielded variable
      read after its channel is closed and reused: "Match the reference" -- which the
      descriptor does for free (FIELD.md's last stated difference is closed).
      ➡️ RESIDUALS (unmeasured on the reference; none is a regression of a gated row):
      (a) `LSET A$=A$` on a fielded A$ -- the source shares the target's bytes and
      is padded before it is copied; (b) whether ERR 50 leaves the overflowing
      variable bound (ours: raised before the store); ~~(c) the row-21 crossing in
      fch_save_active is now a no-op that main still pays for~~ -- ✅ gone with S10.E
      (2026-10-19); (d) scratchpad/wszero_s9_knife.py's K-WS22 / K-WS23 cut
      code that is gone.

          📏 **MEASURED 2026-10-21: THE VG-8020's COLLECTOR IS QUADRATIC, OURS IS
          ~FLAT.** [`gctime_probe.py`](scratchpad/gctime_probe.py) times one
          `FRE("")` (it compacts first) in TIME ticks over N live 8-byte strings
          ([`gctime_run.out`](scratchpad/gctime_run.out)):
          | N | VG-8020, garbage between | VG-8020, none | zerobas |
          |---|---|---|---|
          | 25 | 5 | 5 | 1-2 |
          | 50 | 15 | 15 | 1-2 |
          | 100 | 52 | 54 | 1-2 |
          | 200 | 196 | 196 | 1-2 |
          | 400 | 759 | 760 | 1-2 |

          and the SAME with no garbage at all, so the reference's cost is the scan,
          not the moves: 400 strings is ~15 s per compaction there. zerobas's sorted
          single pass (strheap_gc, 959 B of the sub ROM, 282 of them the sort) does
          it inside one 20 ms tick at every N; `FRE("")` answers 6400 on both.
          🔮 "VG-8020 g.400 / g.100 ~16" HIT (14.6); "zerobas grows 4-5x" UNSCORED
          (below the tick). ➡️ So a quadratic collector -- far smaller -- would still
          be ON PAR (TIER 5's bar); the sort is bytes spent beating the reference by
          ~400x at N=400. The bytes are SUB-ROM bytes (sub page 1 has ~3.9 KB free),
          not the binding main budget.

- [ ] 💽 **D-DISKRUN — THE DISK COLLECTION ON BOTH MACHINES: 18 SYSTEM DISKS REACH
      MSX-DOS ON THE CF-3300 AND BASIC ON zerobas (run 2026-10-21, Joost: "Disk test run")**
      🎚️ TIER 1 — happy path: booting a disk is the first thing a disk machine does.
      🤖 **AUTONOMOUS** — the CF-3300 settles every row; triage is black box (screens,
      CURLIN, PC, our own ROM's breakpoints), the software is RUN, never decoded.
      📏 [`diskcorpus_run.py`](scratchpad/diskcorpus_run.py) boots every image of the `disks`
      collection (Joost 2026-10-20: never `my_disks`, which is private; the tool refuses
      it; the collection's location is passed in, never written here) on the National
      CF-3300 and on zerobas's disk machine from a /tmp copy, 45 s throttle-off, then types
      FILES. 143 images (130 .dsk, 10 .di1/.di2, 3 .xsa; one "*.dsk" entry is a directory):
      | class | n | meaning |
      |---|---|---|
      | BOTH-RUN | 92 | both machines run the disk's program (NOT compared further: a Japanese and a European machine draw different screens) |
      | ZB-NOBOOT | 27 | the CF-3300 runs something, zerobas sits at its prompt |
      | FILES-SAME | 8 | both at the prompt, the same FILES listing |
      | FILES-DIFF | 9 | mostly NOISE (the banners' version numbers, 32- vs 40-column wrapping); real candidates: no-waste.dsk (zerobas lists none), facdemo3.di2 (1 against 41), kq.dsk (two missing at the end) |
      | ZB-ONLY | 6 | zerobas runs a program where the CF-3300 sits in direct mode (BREAKER: zerobas at line 10) -- read each |
      | FILES-EMPTY | 1 | |
      🔴 **CLASS A (18 of the 27 ZB-NOBOOT): the CF-3300 reaches MSX-DOS's `Enter date` and
      zerobas BASIC** -- including disks whose root directory holds NO system file at all
      (empty.dsk has no entries; almost_real.dsk's "directory" is art text). zerobas reads
      those directories CORRECTLY (FILES lists exactly what is there), and the BPBs are the
      test disk's (720 KB, F9) -- so it is not the FAT layer. Both machines enter the disk's
      boot code twice at $C01E (CF=0, then CF=1) identically (a breakpoint on our own call).
      ⚖️ The differential that places it: empty.dsk on the CF-3300 HARDWARE with zerobas's
      disk ROM fitted (`National_CF-3300_ZEROBASDISK`) ends in BASIC with `Type mismatch in
      0`; with the stock disk ROM, `Enter date`. So the divergence is in disk.rom's BOOT path
      (what the boot code is given, or calls, after step 7), not in C-BIOS or BASIC.

- [x] ✅ **DONE 2026-10-23 (D-KEYREP)** ⌨️ **D-KEYREP — THE FIRST KEY AFTER AN IDLE SPELL CAN COME OUT TWICE: A NEW KEY DOES NOT
      RESTART THE AUTO-REPEAT DELAY (found 2026-10-23 by D-STEP7DATE's apparatus)**
      🎚️ TIER 1 — typing at the prompt (a candidate: measure the reference first).
      🤖 **AUTONOMOUS** — work-area cells only.
      📏 lof's `rand_put` with its zerobas lines moved 4 s later typed `PPUT #1,1` and `RRUN`,
      deterministically ([`step7c_lof_v.out`](scratchpad/step7c_lof_v.out)). Sampled every
      20 ms ([`step7c_keyrep.out`](scratchpad/step7c_keyrep.out)): REPCNT (`$F3F7`) sat at 1
      while no key was down; `P` went down (one character queued), was still down at the next
      scan 60 ms later, REPCNT ran out -> a REPEAT (a second `P`), and only then did REPCNT
      reload to 5. The key was down ~120 ms -- a human press. The keys after it did not double:
      REPCNT was already reloaded. lof's 2026 note ("at 9.0 s zerobas began DOUBLING the first
      character") is this, filed then as cadence and paced around.
      ➡️ Measure what the VG-8020 + NMS 1200 does to REPCNT on a NEW key (the work area, while
      a key is held 120 ms after an idle spell), and whether it ever doubles; then the C-BIOS
      key scan (cbios-repack/, a patch) restarts the delay on a new key the same way. Which
      states leave REPCNT at 1 is part of the measurement (it read 0 at the date prompt).
      ✅ **FIXED 2026-10-23 -- AND THE FILED MECHANISM WAS WRONG.** [`keyrep_probe.py`](scratchpad/keyrep_probe.py)
      (keys held on the matrix after idle spells, the work area every 20 ms): a plain 120 ms
      tap queues ONE character on zerobas too, with or without SHIFT, disk or no disk
      ([`keyrep_run2.out`](scratchpad/keyrep_run2.out), [`keyrep_run3.out`](scratchpad/keyrep_run3.out)).
      The doubling is a RACE in C-BIOS's repeat pass (read: C-BIOS source, the repack's own
      base): with KEYBUF empty and REPCNT run out it clears OLDKEY, READS the matrix a second
      time, then sets REPCNT = 1 -- a key that went down between the two reads is queued there,
      its new-key delay overwritten by the 1, so it repeats at the next scan. And the delay
      itself was wrong: both references load REPCNT = **13** on a new key (VG-8020 14 characters
      in a 1.5 s hold at 50 Hz, CF-3300 19 at 60 Hz -- [`keyrep_run.out`](scratchpad/keyrep_run.out),
      [`keyrep_run_cf.out`](scratchpad/keyrep_run_cf.out)), C-BIOS 5 (22 characters).
      Fix: `cbios-repack/key-repeat.patch` (#12): the repeat pass compares the matrix just read
      (`key_cmp`, a label after key_in's read loop) and the delay is 13. 2 bytes change
      ($194A, $19B9), nothing moves; repacked sha1 eaf3fae8. After
      ([`keyrep_after.out`](scratchpad/keyrep_after.out)): 14 characters in 1.5 s on both
      repack machines, every tap 1; lof's shifted timeline now echoes `PUT #1,1` once and
      LOF 256 (the raced key is taken a scan later, as a new key with REPCNT 13).
      🔮 Scored: "zerobas doubles a 120 ms tap after idle" MISS (it does not: a race, not a state);
      "SHIFT is the trigger" MISS; "the disk machine differs" MISS; "after the fix: 14 / 1"
      HIT; "PUT echoed once" HIT.

      FNA(X)=X+1:B=5`, then VARTAB / ARYTAB / VARPTR(B)): the CF-3300's variable area is 29 B
      with B's value at VARTAB+13; zerobas's 24 B, B at VARTAB+8 -- two 5-byte entries before B
      there, one here. Blocker (five DEF FNs) reads 185 B against 134 B at the same lines.
      zerobas keeps FN definitions in its own pool (D-DEFFN, 2026-08-23); Joost's 09-11 ruling
      is about the string-FN GC root taking the pool, NOT about where a definition lives -- read
      [[joost-ruled-merge-and-pool]] before designing. ➡️ Read the reference's entry bytes
      (variable-area RAM: type byte, name, the 2-byte value) to learn what the entry holds; then
      decide whether zerobas mirrors it.

      (our program PRINTs the first 28 bytes from VARTAB; interpreter data, no code): zerobas
      DOES hold the FN entry (`C1 00 02 0F 80`, same size as the VG-8020's `02 C1 00 0F 80`; the
      byte ORDER inside an entry is a documented difference, docs/concepts/variables.md). What
      it lacked were the FORMALS: the VG-8020 creates each one at the DEF, zero-valued, after
      the FN entry -- `(X,Y)` makes X then Y, an existing Y stays put, `(X,X)` makes X once,
      `X!` / `Y#` / `X$` by suffix or DEFtype, and `(C(1))` DIMs an ARRAY C at the DEF
      ([`deffnvar_cases.out`](scratchpad/deffnvar_cases.out)). Fix: ex_deffn walks the formals
      with LET's own lookup (var_name_key, var_alloc_or_find; type 1 for a string name),
      raising nothing (o.lazybody / o.noeq / o.aryformal hold) and stopping at a non-letter or
      at a name followed by `(` (+52 B of the $6CF3 pin pad; page 1's tail unchanged). After:
      every case but the array formal as the VG-8020 ([`deffnvar_after.out`](scratchpad/deffnvar_after.out));
      kwram's four DEF / FN rows now agree on FRE(0) (22 / 22, 12 / 12;
      [`deffnvar_kwram.out`](scratchpad/deffnvar_kwram.out)).
      🧪 deffn-acceptance rows o.defvar / o.defvar2 / o.defvarx: 15 / 24 / 15 on the VG-8020,
      the CF-3300 and zerobas ([`deffnvar_gate.out`](scratchpad/deffnvar_gate.out)).
      🔪 K-DFV1 (the scan skipped): o.defvar 10, o.defvar2 11, o.defvarx 15 (its formal
      exists) -- HIT ([`deffnvar_knife.out`](scratchpad/deffnvar_knife.out)).
      🔴 **AND THE GATE COULD NOT FAIL ON A SUBJECT ROW.** `--gate` fails on controls and
      predicates only; DIFF rows needed `--strict`, which the Makefile never passed -- the
      "until the verb ships" setting, left on since 2026-08-23. All 76 rows agree today
      ([`deffn_strict.out`](scratchpad/deffn_strict.out)), so deffn-acceptance is `--strict`
      now; the knife through `make deffn-acceptance` exits 2.
      🔮 Scored: "zerobas has no FN entry" (the item's own claim) MISS; "the formals are the

      $F7F6, ARG $F847), ch. 2 eight interpreter internals for CALL-statement
      extensions (CHRGTR $4666, FRMEVL $4C64, FRMQNT $542F, GETBYT $521C, FRESTR

      project: ~80 pinned entries across $268C-$67D0, part inside the repacked
      C-BIOS region, some 1 B apart (FOUT $3425 / PUFOUT $3426), and the float
      core's format differs from DAC's BCD (D-ROMSIZE step 4 meets it).

- [ ] 🎚️ **~~TIER 5~~ TIER 4 (SWAPPED 2026-09-24) IS NOW "MATCHES THE REFERENCE'S
      RAM USAGE" — THE RUNG, AND WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE IN IT (D-TIER5RAM,
      2026-09-22)**
      🎚️ TIER 4 — the rung's own definition; it is the bar every other item at
      this tier is measured against.
      🏗️ **SWAPPED WITH SPEED BY JOOST, 2026-09-24 (D-TIERSWAP): RAM USAGE IS
      TIER 4, ON-PAR SPEED IS TIER 5.** He asked whether the two should swap;
      the case put to him was (1) a RAM difference can stop a program RUNNING
      (a listing that fits on the reference is `Out of memory` here, or a
      `CLEAR`/`BLOAD`/`POKE` into a cell we use differently corrupts us) where a
      speed difference mostly makes it slower; (2) with T4 ruled *"track the
      ratio, set no bar yet"* the speed tier cannot CLOSE, and under
      "lowest tier first" an unclosable tier would hold the RAM tier back
      indefinitely. He chose the swap. **Prose below dated 2026-09-22/23 says
      "TIER 5" for this rung — that is the numbering of its date.**
      🏗️ **WHAT THE RUNG SECURES — RULED BY JOOST, 2026-09-24, ALL THREE:**
      asked which of three goals *"matches the reference's RAM usage"* means,
      since they can pull against each other, he chose every one:
      | goal | what it secures | measured by |
      |---|---|---|
      | **(a) same free memory** | `FRE(0)`/`FRE("")` and what `CLEAR` leaves match, so a program that fits on the reference fits here | the OBSERVABLE half |
      | **(b) same addresses** | work-area cells, undocumented ones included, live where the reference keeps them, so `PEEK`/`POKE`/`BLOAD` programs that touch them behave the same | the FOOTPRINT half |
      | **(c) same economy** | zerobas writes no more cells than the reference for the same operation — his *"very economical"* hunch, which stays a prediction to SCORE | the FOOTPRINT half |
      🎯 **AND THE TARGET WHEN THE REFERENCES DIVERGE IS THE VG-8020** — his
      words, *"if the references diverge, prefer the vg8020"*, the same rule
      as style splits [[oracle-split-prefer-vg8020]]. Cells that exist only
      with a disk ROM, which the VG-8020 does not have, take the CF-3300.
      This answers the *"no single referent"* objection below: "exactly" is
      still not the bar, but there IS now one machine to match.
      ⚠️ **WHERE (a) AND (b) CONFLICT** — matching an address can cost free
      memory, or the reverse — **that conflict comes back to Joost**, like
      every adjustment this rung proposes.
      🏗️ **RULED BY JOOST, 2026-09-22.** He proposed a tier *"matches the RAM
      usage of the reference exactly"*, then: ***"it would make more sense to
      make it tier 5 and bump current tier 5 to tier 6"***. Done — 13 `🎚️`
      markers moved, `tier_table.py` has six rungs, and **TIER 6 is now
      "handles every error situation correctly"**. He placed RAM fidelity ABOVE
      exhaustive error handling deliberately.
      ❌ **"EXACTLY" IS NOT THE BAR, AND HE AGREED — THE REFERENCES DISAGREE WITH
      EACH OTHER.** Measured in this tree: the CF-3300 and the Philips NMS 1200
      differ by **+2** in the file-buffer pointer (`expansion-protocol.md`
      §6.6ae), and the VG-8020 and CF-3300 have different stack tops (`$F09E`
      vs `$DB95`, the `VARPTR(#n)` item). *"The reference's RAM usage"* has no
      single referent to match, so a bar of *exact* equality is not well formed.
      ✅ **HIS ADDITION, AND IT WIDENS THE RUNG BEYOND WHAT I PROPOSED:** *"I do
      think we can also see what undocumented region gets used and should also
      try to match that."* So the rung is **not** limited to the documented work
      area — which cells the reference touches in its OWN workspace is in scope
      too, as a target to match where we reasonably can.
      🔴 **CLEAN ROOM, AND THIS IS THE LINE THAT MAKES THE WIDENING LEGAL.**
      Work-area RAM **addresses and CONTENTS are readable** (`expansion-protocol.md`
      §7), and that covers undocumented cells just as much as documented ones —
      *observing which addresses get written is not decoding anything*. What
      stays forbidden is §8.5: **the BYTES of the reference's RAM-RESIDENT CODE**.
      A written cell inside one of those five clusters is therefore reported as
      *belonging to a cluster*, never decoded. ROM bytes remain out entirely.
      ➡️ **THE BAR, IN TWO HALVES, BECAUSE THEY HAVE DIFFERENT EVIDENCE:**
      **(i) OBSERVABLE** — what a BASIC program can see: `FRE(0)`, `FRE("")`,
      `VARPTR` deltas, `PEEK` of documented cells, what `CLEAR n` leaves. These
      are behavioural and belong to the keyword that exposes them.
      **(ii) FOOTPRINT** — which cells get written for a given operation, in both
      workspaces. Measured by the watchpoint method, not by reading code.
      ⚠️ **AND A CAUTION ABOUT PLACEMENT THAT THE RENUMBER DOES NOT REMOVE:** an
      observable RAM divergence can break an ORDINARY program — `PEEK(VARPTR(A$))`
      is not exotic in MSX-land. When one does, it deserves the tier its IMPACT
      earns, which may be TIER 1, not this rung. The rung is where the SYSTEMATIC
      comparison lives, not a place to park breakage.
      🤖 **AUTONOMOUS** — the MEASUREMENT is permitted and needs no ruling. ⚠️ Any
      ADJUSTMENT it proposes comes back to Joost: moving a cell to match the
      reference changes an address this tree has already made decisions about
      (`docs/sysvar-rehoming-decisions.md`).

      what WE declare. A cell the reference writes that we never named is the
      interesting direction, and so is a cell we reserve that it never touches.

      code (§8.5) — so a cell inside one of those five clusters is reported as

      🔬 **D-RAMFOOT, THE FIRST MEASUREMENT (2026-09-24,
      `scratchpad/ramfoot_probe.py`, `scratchpad/ramfoot_run.out`).** 16
      one-line operations, VG-8020 vs zerobas, every address in `$E001..$FFFF`
      written inside a window the program opens and closes itself
      (`POKE&HE000,201/202`, keyed by a per-case TAG so a lost window cannot
      shift the rows). Stack pushes are classified by SP and excluded; an empty
      window gives the background; a positive `POKE&HE001,7` must record
      `$E001` on both or the run REFUSES. **Deterministic** — two runs diff
      identical.
      🔴 **THE INTERRUPT HAD TO BE MEASURED, NOT GUESSED, AND TWO CLASSIFIERS
      FAILED FIRST.** zerobas takes 8–14 ms from the TIME tick to its window,
      so nearly every zerobas window holds a 50 Hz interrupt (H.TIMI hits are
      counted per window). "Written only with interrupts off" caught
      interpreter cells (zerobas writes `ARYTAB`/`FRETOP`/`CTLLIM` under DI),
      and "near a tick" per op caught `FORCLR` on `COLOR`. What works is an
      `isr` control: a wait loop spans one tick, and a cell EVERY write of
      which sits within 0.3 ms before to 3 ms after an H.TIMI hit is the
      interrupt's. **Interrupt signature: VG-8020 31 cells, zerobas 24** —
      `STATFL`, `JIFFY`, the `NEWKEY` rows on both.
      🔮 **JOOST'S HUNCH, SCORED: HIT.** *"The reference writes FEWER distinct
      cells for the same operation"* — **on 12 of 16 ops; 527 cells vs 843
      in total (zerobas 1.6×)**. The four exceptions: `PRINT 1` (39 vs 8),
      `CLS` (69 vs 26), `LOCATE` (5 vs 4), `STR$` (47 vs 42). My own
      prediction (fewer `$F380+` cells here, more in total, not on every op)
      — HIT on all three parts.

      arithmetic, variables and strings the reference writes the DOCUMENTED
      work area (`$F662`, `$F678..`, `$F698..`, `$F6A5..`, `$F6C4..$F6C7`,
      `$F7B4..`, `$F7F6..$F84F` recur), and zerobas writes almost none of it:
      its FAC/ARG/conversion/variable state lives in its OWN workspace

      state there and zerobas's stale bytes — an ADDRESS divergence per cell,
      to be named from the MSX2 TH work-area table and cross-checked against

      ➕ **zerobas also writes `SLTTBL3` (`$FCC8`) and the secondary-slot
      register `$FFFF` on most ops** — its sub-ROM tenant calls; the reference

- [ ] 🔴 **`refcache-check` GOES RED ON THE CALENDAR, AND THE RETRY ARM CALLS IT
      "REAL".**
      🎚️ APPARATUS — a time-dependent red is indistinguishable from a
      regression at the moment you have to decide whether to commit.
      🤖 **AUTONOMOUS** — no ruling needed.
      Observed 2026-09-19: a full `make gates` reported `rc=2 refcache-check`,
      retried it, printed **`retry refcache-check: rc 2->2  REAL (still red)`**
      and failed the battery. The suite then passed STANDALONE, and passed again
      under the battery's own `ZEROBAS_REFCACHE=0`, so the environment was not
      the cause.
      🔴 **THE CAUSE IS THE CLOCK.** `probes/lib/probe_refcache.py --maintain`
      reported `oldest 14.0d, cap 14d; pruned 27` on the first standalone run
      and `pruned 0` on the next: the store had aged PAST its 14-day cap during
      the battery, and the run that diagnosed it also REPAIRED it. A second full
      battery was then 42/42 green with `refcache-check rc=0`.
      ⚠️ **THE RETRY ARM IS THE PART THAT MISLEADS.** It exists to separate flakes
      from regressions, and it reported this one as REAL because a second run
      inside the same battery is a second run at the same instant — a boundary
      condition is not a race. A retry that cannot move the clock cannot classify
      a clock-driven red.
      ⚠️ **AND A GREEN RE-RUN WAS GREEN FOR THE WRONG REASON** — the prune had
      already fixed it [[a-case-that-agrees-can-agree-for-the-wrong-reason]].
      🟢 **PARTIAL 2026-09-19 (D-REFRACE) — ONE PROVEN MECHANISM REMOVED, AND
      THE ORIGINAL RED STILL NOT EXPLAINED.** `maintain()` walked the store
      TWICE, pruning against one `time.time()` and then measuring ages against a
      later one, so its own post-condition (*"after a prune no entry may be past
      the cap"*) could fail an entry that the prune had legitimately kept. One
      clock reading is now threaded through `_age`/`expired`/`prune`/
      `store_stats`, so the two walks cannot disagree about what time it is.
      🔴 **BUT THAT IS ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT WHAT WAS OBSERVED, AND SAYING SO IS
      THE POINT.** The gap between the two walks is MICROSECONDS; for it to
      matter an entry must sit within microseconds of the cap. The filed red had
      27 entries pruned and `oldest 14.0d` — plausible for a store aging out,
      not for a microsecond window. So this removes a mechanism that is provably
      red-capable, and does NOT close the item.
      ⚠️ **AND THE FIRST ARM I WROTE FOR IT WAS VACUOUS.** KA11 planted an entry
      half a second under the cap and asserted `maintain()` green — it passes
      with or without the fix, which a mutation reverting `prune(now=now)`
      DEMONSTRATED by leaving it passing. It is relabelled as a green control.
      KA12 is the arm with content: measure the post-condition a second later
      than the prune — the shape the code had — and the same store goes RED.
      🟢 **CANDIDATES TESTED 2026-09-19 (D-REFDIAG) — ONE REPRODUCES, ONE IS
      REFUTED, AND THE FILED INCIDENT IS STILL UNEXPLAINED.**
      🔴 **Candidate 1 REPRODUCES ON DEMAND:** an over-cap entry whose unlink
      fails (read-only parent directory) is counted by `except OSError: kept +=
      1` and is then INDISTINGUISHABLE from a legitimately young entry —
      `maintain()` goes red saying only *"an entry survived the prune"*, with no
      path, no age for the offender, and no hint that a delete failed.
      🟢 **Candidate 2 is REFUTED BY CONSTRUCTION, not by a test:** a concurrent
      writer cannot produce this symptom at all. `store()` writes through
      `mkstemp` + `os.replace`, so every entry it creates has a FRESH mtime and
      an age of ~0. A parallel suite can race the walk but cannot manufacture an
      over-cap entry.
      ⚠️ **NEITHER EXPLAINS THE FILED RED**, whose survivor sat at `oldest 14.0d`
      and pruned cleanly on the next run. So the item stays OPEN — but the next
      occurrence will name its own cause instead of needing reconstruction: the
      red now prints WHICH entry survived, its age to four decimals, its margin
      over the cap in seconds, and whether its unlink FAILED (`PRUNE_FAILED`,
      with the errno). The run that investigates it will no longer be the run
      that destroys the evidence.
      🔴 **AND A LARGER FINDING ABOUT MY OWN METHOD, WHICH COST A WRONG CLAIM.**
      D-REFRACE reported "KA11 is vacuous — a mutation reverting `prune(now=now)`
      left it PASSING". That conclusion was right and the EVIDENCE WAS NOT: the
      mutation was applied to a COPY of the file, and this module's selftest does
      `import probe_refcache as RC` (line ~617, deliberately — it tests the
      instance `omsx_repl` will use), so the copy's own code was never under
      test. **`assert the source changed` is necessary and NOT sufficient; the
      mutated code must BE the code under test.** Mutating IN PLACE and restoring
      afterwards shows the truth: reverting the one-clock fix made NO arm fail —
      KA12 passes `stats_now` by hand, so it exercises the shape without ever
      checking that `maintain` threads its clock into `prune`. **D-REFRACE's fix
      shipped UNCOVERED.**
      🟢 **KA15 covers it now**, and a mutation confirms it bites: plant a
      20-day-old entry, run `maintain` against a clock 30 days in the PAST, and
      the entry must SURVIVE (its age is negative at that clock). Revert
      `prune(now=now)` and it is deleted. Its negative control runs the same
      entry at the real clock and requires it to be pruned, so the arm is about
      the clock and not about expiry being broken.
      🟢 **✅ THE MISLEADING-VERDICT HALF IS FIXED 2026-09-21 (D-RETRYSUBJ) —
      AND BOTH VERDICTS WERE WRONG, NOT ONE.** The item said *"a retry that
      cannot move the clock cannot classify a clock-driven red"*; the deeper rule
      is that **a retry is only evidence when the first run did not change the
      subject**. `refcache-check`'s recipe ends `probe_refcache.py --maintain`,
      and maintain PRUNES — so the red run is also a REPAIRING run.
      * **Still red → not REAL**: a second run inside the same battery is a
        second run at the same instant.
      * **Green on retry → not FLAKE**: the first run fixed it, and counting that
        as a recovered flake launders a real repair
        [[a-case-that-agrees-can-agree-for-the-wrong-reason]]. A fix that caught
        only the red half would have left this one standing.
      `tools/run_gates.py` gained `SELF_REPAIRING` + `retry_verdict()`: such a
      target reads **INCONCLUSIVE** in BOTH directions and is never added to the
      recovered-flakes list. ⚠️ **The battery's pass/fail is UNCHANGED** — rc is
      still rc; only the CLAIM about what the rc means is corrected.
      🔴 **MEMBERSHIP IS EARNED BY THE RECIPE, NOT ASSERTED:** arm S18 runs
      `make -n` on every member and requires a mutating flag in its own recipe,
      so the set cannot rot into a list of targets someone wanted to stop
      failing. Six arms (S13–S18); S15/S16/S17 verified to go RED with
      `SELF_REPAIRING` emptied **in the module under test**, which is the
      mutation discipline this item's own D-REFRACE entry had to learn.
      ⚠️ **THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE FILED RED IS STILL OPEN** — this fixes what the
      battery SAYS about it, not why the store aged out. The item stays open.

| tier | per keyword | test |
|---|---|---|
| **TIER 1** | works correctly in the happy path | a MISSING keyword is TIER 1, not "unimplemented" |
| **TIER 2** | works in reasonable time | usable; not yet on par |
| **TIER 3** | handles the most common error situations | *would a 1985 magazine listing plausibly hit this?* — Type mismatch, Syntax error, Illegal function call on a bad argument, File not found, Out of DATA, Subscript out of range, Division by zero, a forgotten disk |
| **TIER 4** | matches the reference's RAM usage | not "exactly" — the references disagree with each other (D-TIER5RAM); per keyword it is DERIVED from the whole-RAM-map comparison |
| **TIER 5** | faster than or on par with the reference | the baseline is NOT 1.0 (D-INTERPSPEED §4); T5 rows RECORD the ratio and set no bar yet (Joost, 2026-09-24) |
| **TIER 6** | handles every error situation correctly | nesting depth 11, `+$$###`, string-temp-stack overflow, which of two errors wins |

**2026-09-10:** five tiers, TIER 4 = speed, TIER 5 = every error.
**2026-09-22:** RAM usage inserted as TIER 5, every error bumped to TIER 6.
**2026-09-24 (D-TIERSWAP):** RAM and speed swapped — TIER 4 = RAM usage,
TIER 5 = speed. So a "TIER 5" dated before 09-22 means every error, one dated

🌱 **BREADTH BEGINS (D-KWBREADTH batch 1, 2026-09-13) — the OTHER half of what
establishing a tier needs, and the half no keyword has.**
| row | reading | the form it adds |
|---|---|---|
| `sgn_b` | `[-1 0 1]` | all THREE sign branches — a row taking only `SGN(5)` passes on an implementation that never returns −1 |
| `fix_b` | `[-2 2]` | truncation toward zero on BOTH signs, where `FIX` and `INT` differ |
| `cos_b` | `[ 1 ]` | the exact point of the cosine |
| `vpoke_b` | `[ 7 ]` | the **LAST** byte of a 16 KB VRAM, where the existing row uses address 0 — an off-by-one in the address path shows here and nowhere else |
| `vpoke_b2` | `[ 255 ]` | the maximum byte VALUE, where the existing row writes 9 |
🎯 **EVERY READING IS A VALUE, NOT AN ERROR** (mode 6, learned from `PAD` the
same day), and none is 0 on both sides, which would merely trade mode 6 for
mode 2. **`vpoke_b` is KNIFE-PROVEN CONNECTED** — breadth that would notice a
break, not another agreement point.
⚠️ **AND THE LIMIT, SO FIVE ROWS DO NOT READ AS FIVE EQUAL PIECES OF
EVIDENCE**: `SGN`, `FIX` and `COS` are among the **30 keywords the knife
REFUSES** — the math and string groups dispatch through a third shape it
cannot reach — so their connectedness is UNMEASURABLE until that cut exists.
Their rows are breadth; they are not yet breadth that is known to bite.
🔬 **AND A REUSABLE LESSON: THE 38-COLUMN GUARD MEASURES THE TYPED LINE, BUT
WHAT WRAPS IS THE LINE PLUS WHATEVER THE SCREEN ALREADY HOLDS.** `vpoke_b2`
cleared the guard at 37 characters, PASSED when run alone, and lost its echo
anchor entirely once other rows had run before it — `UNREADABLE`, with the
reference showing a wrap pipe (`|[ 255 ]`). **A row that passes in isolation
and fails in company is precisely why the whole sweep summary gets read**, and
why `ONLY=` is a debugging aid rather than a verdict. Both `VPOKE` rows are
stored-mode now and the reason is recorded ON THE ROW, where the next author
meets it.
🌱 **BREADTH BATCH 2 (D-KWBREADTH, 2026-09-13) — AND THIS TIME THE TARGETS
WERE MEASURED, NOT GUESSED.** Batch 1 was aimed by intuition and landed on the
WELL-covered end: `make kwcover` over a full **83-suite / 46 969-line** capture
(0 of 159 keywords UNEXERCISED) puts `STR$` at 18 suites, `MID$` 14, `STRING$`
13, `HEX$` 10, `OCT$` 7, `INSTR` 6, `RND` 5. The planned batch-2 list was every
one of those. 🎯 **THE THIN END IS EIGHT KEYWORDS TYPED BY `kwsweep` PLUS
EXACTLY ONE OTHER SUITE — `ATTR$ BSAVE CALL CMD CVD DELETE IPL SET` — AND THAT
ONE SUITE IS `lnblank-acceptance` FOR ALL EIGHT, WHICH TYPES THEM AS TOKENISER
SUBJECTS (`20 CALL X`, `20 CALLX5`, `20 CALL X+5`) AND NEVER EXECUTES ONE.** So
those eight have ONE scoring row each; the MK/CV family sits just above at 3-4
suites with the same shape, and its existing rows have a visible reach limit:
`CVI(MKI$(7))` uses a value whose high byte is 0 and whose sign bit is clear,
so neither a byte swap nor a sign error can show; `CVS(MKS$(1))` and
`CVD(MKD$(1))` use a value that survives almost any mantissa packing; and
`LEN(MKI$(1))=2`, `LEN(MKS$(1))=4`, `LEN(MKD$(1))=8` **are all passed by a stub
that returns the right number of ZERO bytes.**
| row | reading | the form it adds |
|---|---|---|
| `cvi_b` | `[-1  32767 ]` | the SIGN and the 16-bit EXTREME, neither reachable through 7 |
| `cvs_b` | `[ 1.5 ]` | a FRACTION, on the 4-byte single pack |
| `cvd_b` | `[ .1 ]` | a fraction with NO exact binary form, on the 8-byte double pack |
| `mki_b` | `[ 2 ]` | MKI$'s **CONTENT** where its own row scores only LENGTH; 258 is `$0102`, so both bytes are non-zero and the reading confirms the little-endian order `basic/sysvars.inc:252` documents |
🔪 **THREE OF THE FOUR ARE KNIFE-PROVEN LOAD-BEARING** (`CVI`, `CVS`, `CVD` all
went MISSING with the selector cut) — a real improvement on batch 1, where
`SGN`/`FIX`/`COS` were all unmeasurable. Sweep: `DIVERGENT=2 SUPPORTED=188`,
the two divergences still the expected `swap_t3`/`dskf_t3` pair.
🔬 **AND `MKI$`'s REFUSAL IS THE FIRST CONCRETE LEAD ON THE 30**: the knife
reports *0 `cp $AE` sites with an `ev_*` target, 0 occurrences in
`ev_ff_argtab`*, and `basic/sysvars.inc:250` says why in prose written long
before the knife existed — **MKI$ is evaluated in `basic/strvar.asm` because it
returns a STRING**. The third cut shape is not one mystery, it is the
STRING-RETURNING function path, and that is a searchable target rather than a
tally.
📏 **THE PER-KEYWORD COST, WHICH IS THE NUMBER THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS SCALES
TO 159**: one full sweep and one knife invocation covered the WHOLE batch, so
machine time is per-BATCH, not per-keyword, and amortises away. The irreducible
cost is DESIGN — read the existing row, then find a form it cannot reach — and
that is minutes per keyword and does not parallelise onto the machine. **So
breadth scales, and the binding constraint is authorship, not wall time.**
🌾 **BREADTH BATCH 3 (D-KWBREADTH, 2026-09-14) — A NEGATIVE RESULT, AND IT CLOSES
THE THIN-EIGHT LINE WITH A MEASURED REASON.** 🔴 **THIN COVERAGE AND *BROADENABLE*
COVERAGE ARE NOT THE SAME THING.** `kwcover` ranks by EXERCISE, and a keyword can
be thin **because there is nothing to exercise** — so the screening step is
reading each candidate's EXISTING row, and it is the cheap step that saves the
expensive one.
| of the thin eight | why breadth cannot help |
|---|---|
| `SET` `IPL` `CMD` | refuse ON SIGHT — ERR 5 on **every** reference; no working behaviour exists to broaden |
| `CALL` | its row tests that the word is RESERVED, which exercises the TOKENISER, not a handler |
| `ATTR$` | its exec line is `None` (MSX-DOS2-era, measured for the record) |
| `BSAVE` | **already** breadth-quality: a round trip, POKE 99 → BSAVE → overwrite with 7 → BLOAD → read 99 back |
| `CVD` | done in batch 2 |
| `DELETE` | the one real candidate — and it was MEASURED, not assumed |
🔬 **`DELETE` OF AN EXISTING LINE SILENTLY TERMINATES THE PROGRAM** — no error, no
output — and **all three machines agree**, both references included
(`scratchpad/deleterange_probe.py`, VG-8020 · CF-3300 · zerobas). The no-delete
CONTROL prints `[C9]` on all three, so the harness and the program shape are sound
and the silence is `DELETE`'s own doing; `DELETE 30-40` over existing lines behaves
the same. 🎯 **So its success path CANNOT CARRY A VALUE READING: a row for it
would read NOTHING ON BOTH SIDES, which is mode 2** — trading one blind spot for
another, which is the trade `PAD` already taught. **The thin eight yield ZERO
broadenable rows, and that is now a measurement rather than an omission.**
✅ **AND ONE USEFUL BY-PRODUCT, because the `AUTO` hazard was the reason to check:
`DELETE` RETURNS CLEANLY TO THE `Ok` PROMPT** — the `color auto goto list run`
function-key line is intact in every capture — so unlike `AUTO` (which left the
machine in LINE-ENTRY MODE and swallowed the input of 21 following rows) it would
NOT have poisoned its neighbours. The hazard was real in kind, absent in this case.
🔴 **AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN IS THE LESSON WORTH KEEPING: REUSE THE EXISTING
TABLE, DO NOT INVENT YOUR OWN.** It supplied its own boot/reset values instead of
`basic_probe_kwsweep`'s `MACH_BOOT`/`MACH_RESET_PRE`, so the CF-3300 booted into
SCREEN 1 and every capture was the **PATTERN GENERATOR TABLE read as text** —
byte-identical for all four cases, **which is exactly what a broken leg looks like
when you want a result**. `omsx_repl` REFUSED TO CACHE IT AND SAID WHY rather than
handing back a plausible string. `basic_probe_kwsweep.py:1872` already records that
these two tables disagreeing "is what let this sit"; this probe reproduced that
exact failure by not reusing the one that exists.
🌾 **BREADTH BATCH 4 (D-KWBREADTH, 2026-09-14) — AND THE SCREEN THAT FOUND IT IS
THE REUSABLE PART.** Two row shapes predict an untouched behaviour far better than
any coverage RANK: **(a) a row that scores an ERROR leaves the SUCCESS path
untouched; (b) a row that scores a LENGTH or an EXISTENCE leaves the CONTENT
untouched** — which is exactly what `MKI$` turned out to be in batch 2.
⚠️ **AND THE SCREEN ITSELF OVER-FLAGGED, THE SAME WAY THE KNIFE DID.** A regex
looking for `LEN(` named `inkey` a candidate; the row is
`PRINT"[";A$;LEN(A$);"]"` → `[A 1 ]` and prints the CONTENT as well. **Every
candidate was then confirmed by READING its row, not by trusting the filter** —
the third time in one night that my own instrument drew a line I nearly reported
as a property of the tree.
| row | reading | what the old row could not reach |
|---|---|---|
| `using_b` | `[3.15]` | `##` needs no fraction, no point placement and no rounding; `#.##` needs all three, and 3.146 must ROUND to 3.15, not truncate to 3.14 |
| `mks_b` | `[ 65 ]` | MKS$'s CONTENT — `LEN(MKS$(1))=4` is passed by a stub returning four ZERO bytes; 1.5 packs as `65 21 0 0`, measured on the CF-3300 |
| `mkd_b` | `[ 65 ]` | the same reading on the 8-byte DOUBLE pack |
| `input_b` | `[Hello]` | the BYTES, not the COUNT — `LEN(A$)=24` is passed by a read returning 24 BLANKS; `HI.TXT` is `"Hello from zerobas-disk!"` (`tools/make_test_dsk.py`) |
🔪 **THREE OF THE FOUR ARE KNIFE-PROVEN LOAD-BEARING** (`MKS$`, `MKD$`, `INPUT`).
⚠️ **`USING` IS UNMEASURABLE, AND FOR A STRUCTURAL REASON WORTH RECORDING: token
`$E4` IS NOT IN `stmt_table` AT ALL** — `USING` is a MODIFIER of `PRINT`, not a
dispatched statement, so the statement cut cannot reach it by construction, the
way `ELSE` and `TO` cannot. That is a THIRD unconnectable-by-construction shape
beside `CALL`/`MAX` (reservedness) and it is a property of the language, not a
gap in the knife.
📏 Sweep `DIVERGENT=2 SUPPORTED=192`, the two divergences still the expected
`swap_t3`/`dskf_t3` pair, no `UNREADABLE`.
🌾 **BREADTH BATCH 5 (D-KWBREADTH, 2026-09-14) — THE CONSTANT-MARKER SHAPE, AND A
THIRD DIVERGENCE THAT WAS NOT A DEFECT.** Screening every row (not just
single-row keywords) found **twenty that print only a CONSTANT MARKER**: they
score that the word RAN and nothing about what it DID. Some are legitimate — for
`IF`/`THEN`/`ELSE` the marker's IDENTITY is which branch was taken — but where the
effect is separately readable, the marker is the whole of the evidence.
| row | reading | the effect its marker could not see |
|---|---|---|
| `clear_b` | `[ 1 ]` | `CLEAR` really RESETS variables — `A=5:CLEAR:A=A+1` reads 1, where a CLEAR that did nothing leaves 6. `clearkw` prints `[5]` |
| `locate_b` | `[N 5 ]` | the **ROW** argument, read back through `CSRLIN`. `locate` sets only a COLUMN and scores the marker's INDENTATION |
🔪 Both **knife-proven LOAD-BEARING**. Sweep back to `DIVERGENT=2 SUPPORTED=194`.
🔴 **AND `locate_b` WALKED INTO A WARNING SITTING TWO ROWS AWAY FROM IT.** Written
plainly it came back **DIVERGENT — and the VALUES AGREED**: ref `|||[ 5 ]` vs zb
`||||[ 5 ]`, three wrap pipes against four. `LOCATE` MOVES THE CURSOR, so the blank
lines ahead of the output depend on ambient screen state and **the row was
measuring SCREEN GEOMETRY rather than the keyword.** The `csrlin` row below it
already carries both the diagnosis (*"the VALUE is ambient scroll state"*) and the
remedy (*"Anchored with CLS all three agree everywhere"*). 🎯 **A THIRD DIVERGENCE
IS A NEW FINDING — AND THE FINDING WAS ABOUT MY ROW, NOT THE INTERPRETER.
INVESTIGATE BEFORE FILING, ALWAYS: the values matching while the verdict says
DIVERGENT is the signature of an APPARATUS difference.**
⚠️ **AND THE `CLS` THEN COST THE ECHO — THE NEXT TRAP IN THE SAME CORNER.**
Anchored but untagged, the row read `UNREADABLE ?noecho` on BOTH sides, because
`CLS` erases the echoed command the capture keys on. `NOECHO:` exists for exactly
that; the row is now captured by its own marker `[N` (the free one — `C D G L O Q
R S T W Z` were taken). **Two fixes, each of which created the next problem, and
both were already documented in this file by somebody who had met them.**
🌾 **BREADTH BATCH 6 (D-KWBREADTH, 2026-09-14) — ONE READBACK PATH TURNED TWO
CONSTANT MARKERS INTO VALUES.** `sound` writes PSG register 7 and prints `[7]`;
`outkw` writes the PSG ADDRESS LATCH and prints `[8]`. Neither observes what
landed — and I had written the PSG off as having no readback. **It has one:
`OUT &HA0,<reg>` selects a register and `INP(&HA2)` reads it**, so both effects
are observable and one mechanism served both rows.
| row | reading | the effect its marker could not see |
|---|---|---|
| `sound_b` | `[ 123 ]` | the byte `SOUND` actually DELIVERED, read back out of the PSG |
| `out_b` | `[ 77 ]` | the whole `OUT` → `INP` round trip through the DATA port; `outkw` writes only the ADDRESS latch and never reads it back |
🔪 **Both knife-proven LOAD-BEARING.** Sweep `DIVERGENT=2 SUPPORTED=196`.
⚠️ Register 0 (channel A fine tune) is used rather than 7 because it is a plain
8-bit cell **and because the MIXER is left exactly as it was — nothing is made
audible, and nothing is left changed for the rows that follow** (the `AUTO`
lesson: a row that mutates machine state is a row that can poison its neighbours).
🌾 **BREADTH BATCH 7 (D-KWBREADTH, 2026-09-14) — `BEEP` IS OBSERVABLE TOO, AND
THE CONSTANT-MARKER SCREEN IS NOW COMPLETE.** `beep_b` reads `[ 184 ]`,
**knife-proven LOAD-BEARING**; sweep `DIVERGENT=2 SUPPORTED=197`.
| case (`scratchpad/beepobs_probe.py`, all three machines) | PSG reg 7 |
|---|---|
| at rest — no `SOUND`, no `BEEP` | **184** |
| `SOUND 7,255`, no `BEEP` | **191** (`$BF`, the write masked) |
| `SOUND 7,255` **then** `BEEP` | **184** — BEEP put the mixer back |
🔴 **AND THE FIRST RUN OF THAT PROBE COULD NOT SEE IT: ITS CONTROL READ REGISTER 8
WHILE THE CHANGE WAS IN REGISTER 7.** `184` would have been read as *"nothing
happened"*, and the only thing separating that from the truth was a no-BEEP
reading OF THE SAME CELL. **A CONTROL AIMED AT THE WRONG CELL EXCLUDES NOTHING** —
the `a-case-that-agrees-can-agree-for-the-wrong-reason` rule, applied to the
CONTROL rather than to the case.
📋 **THE CONSTANT-MARKER CLASSIFICATION, FINISHED — so the next author does not
re-derive it.** Four rows gained an EFFECT reading (`clearkw`→`clear_b`,
`locate`→`locate_b`, `sound`→`sound_b`, `outkw`→`out_b`, plus `beep`→`beep_b`);
the rest are blocked, **and every reason was already written in this file**:
| row | why the marker is the honest limit |
|---|---|
| `renum` | its own note: *"RENUM stops the program, so nothing after it runs in the same case"* |
| `waitkw` | its own note: the first attempt BLOCKED FOR EVER BY DEFINITION (mask 0 can never satisfy `((INP(port) XOR xor) AND mask) <> 0`), and zerobas's silence was CORRECT. The one satisfiable port (VDP status bit 7) is READ-TO-CLEAR and would disturb the BIOS interrupt handler |
| `newkw` `deletekw` | program mutators; `DELETE` was MEASURED to terminate the program silently |
| `listkw` | `LIST` prints the PROGRAM while the row's own typed source is already on screen — ambiguous BY CONSTRUCTION |
| `stopkw` `files` `merge` `csave` | the marker sits before a halt or an I/O side effect with no readback in this harness |
🎯 **THIRTEEN BREADTH ROWS ACROSS SEVEN BATCHES, AND THE SCREEN THAT FOUND THEM IS
THE DELIVERABLE**: a row scoring an **ERROR** leaves the SUCCESS path untouched; a
row scoring a **LENGTH or EXISTENCE** leaves the CONTENT untouched; a row scoring a
**CONSTANT MARKER** leaves the EFFECT untouched. ⚠️ **And every screen over-flags,
so each candidate is confirmed by READING its row** — a `LEN(` regex nominated
`inkey`, whose row prints `A$` as well.
🌾 **BREADTH BATCH 8 (D-KWBREADTH, 2026-09-14) — THE FOURTH SCREENING AXIS: A
BOOLEAN READING SCORES A HALF-PLANE, NEVER THE VALUE.** Six rows read `>0`,
`>1000`, `<1` or `>=`, and `VDP(1)>0` is `-1` for ANY non-zero register read — the
note beside it already said the number is **240**, so the value was known and
simply not scored.
| row | reading | what the half-plane hid |
|---|---|---|

mirror, so no row anywhere can witness what the VDP got. The bar is the two ACCESS
PATHS, and the row scores the assignment path — parse, evaluate, store the value
written.

loop's TIME **value** would diverge on INTERPRETER SPEED and be reported as a TIME
defect. `time_c` is where TIME's value gets scored, because writing a known value
and reading it back has no speed dependence. ⚠️ `INT(TIME/100)` and not `TIME`:
the clock ticks between the write and the read, so the raw value is not
reproducible; divided by 100 both readings sit exactly on a multiple and are
stable for ~100 ticks.

— six behaviours, and the three suffix forms really are three: a segment, an
OUTLINED box and a FILLED box are different drawings between the same two points.
The first coordinate is OPTIONAL and continues from the last point (GRPAC), a form
no other graphics verb here has. **N=6 is the widest in the table and it should
be** — LINE has more distinct shapes than any other MSX1 graphics statement.
🎯 **EVERY NEW ROW READS A PIXEL IT MUST DRAW *AND* ONE WHERE THE WRONG READING
WOULD HAVE DRAWN** — not merely somewhere blank, which only proves the screen is
not all 15. `linekw_d` STEP `[0o 15  4 ]`: an ignored STEP draws `(0,0)-(5,0)`, so

omitted start `[0p 15  4 ]`: a start defaulting to (0,0) draws the diagonal

second reading is that diagonal, not empty space. `linekw_f` default colour
`[0q 11  4 ]` from FORCLR.

it is also ON THE DIAGONAL, so a bare segment reads 15 there too. (7,3) is inside,
off the edges and off the diagonal: 15 for a fill, 4 for a `,B` outline **and** 4
for a bare segment, so one reading separates BF from both.

The ADDRESS is machine-specific, so a row must read a DELTA — exactly what

cancels". The references stride at **265**: the MSX-standard FCB, 256-byte record
plus 9 header bytes. Ours would be `FCH_CTXSZ` = `FCH_STATESZ` 50 + `FCH_RECMAX`

and matching it means adopting MSX's FCB shape — a change to the channel
implementation, not to `VARPTR`.

**0.156 ms** (D-XSLOTPRICE), so a 4 KB `LOAD` would gain **~640 ms** of pure
overhead on a machine already ~3× slower than the reference. That is a TIER 2
question — reasonable time — not a free 250 B.

OPERATION. That is a redesign of the channel I/O layer, which is **the same layer
Joost's MSX-FCB-shape ruling already touches**, so the two should be priced
together rather than separately.

| | VG-8020 | zerobas |
|---|---|---|

✅ **THE SUBSTANCE OF THE HYPOTHESIS HOLDS**: 265 is the FCB proper (9 + 256) and
there are **2 MORE BYTES A CHANNEL** charged to `FRE(0)` that are not part of it.
Both numbers were re-measured here rather than inherited, and the FRE charge is
linear over three steps on both machines.
🔴 **BUT THE DECIDING ROW CAME BACK THE OTHER WAY, AND THAT IS THE USEFUL PART.**
I predicted `VARPTR(#1)` would shift by **267** per channel if a `FILTAB` sat
ABOVE the FCBs. It shifts by **265**, and the three readings agree on one
implied constant: **the FCB area's TOP IS PINNED AT `$F380` AND THE ARRAY GROWS
DOWNWARD, with #1 LOWEST** (`VARPTR(#1) + 265n = −3200 = $F380` for n = 1, 2 and
3). So the extra 2 a channel lives **BELOW** the FCB array, not above it — a
guess that fitted the arithmetic and still had the geometry backwards.
🎯 **WHAT THAT PINS FOR THE REBUILD**: match the reference exactly and a channel
costs **265 of FCB + 2 elsewhere**, the array hangs downward off `$F380`, and
`VARPTR(#n) = $F380 − 265·(MAXFILES − n + 1)` falls out for free instead of being
made to agree.
📏 **AND OUR OVERCHARGE IS NOW EXACT**: we charge **306** a channel
(`[state:50][record:256]`) against the reference's 267 — **39 B a channel more
than the reference charges**, of which **41 B** is the per-channel engine state
that has to leave the block (306 − 265). At `MAXFILES=15` the difference is
**585 B** of pool.

output, because the handler's own text contains the marker. The reading is still
unambiguously an error, but a fence that appears in the source it echoes is the
hazard this tree has hit before and the cell is ugly proof of it.

`VARPTR(#n)` then falls out of it agreeing rather than being made to agree.

💰 **THE STRIDE IS THE SMALL HALF. THE 41 BYTES ARE THE WORK.** Our block is
`[state:FCH_STATESZ 50][record:256]` = **306**; the MSX FCB header is **9**. So the
change is finding a home for 41 B of per-channel ENGINE state that MSX keeps
elsewhere — the cluster iterator (`FAT_CURCLUS`/`FAT_CLUSSEC`), the file meta
`LOF` reads (`FAT_FIRSTCLUS`/`FAT_FILESIZE`), the read stream
(`FREAD_OFF`/`FREAD_LEFT`) and the whole `FWR_*` write state
(`basic/sysvars.inc` FCH_STATE0). MSX keeps it in the DISK ROM's work area —
which, after the hook re-architecture, is a place this tree now has.

🎯 **AND THE ROWS EARN N=1 BECAUSE OF WHAT THEIR AUTHORS PUT IN FRONT OF THE
READING, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH RECORDING**: `eof` **reads the file to its end
first**, so the answer is -1 against the 0 a stub gives — asking EOF of a freshly
opened file would have been 0 either way. `loc` consumes a known number of bytes
first. `kill` reads DSKF **before and after** and scores the DIFFERENCE, so it sees
the space the file gave back. `copy` opens the DESTINATION and reads its length.
`readkw` reads, RESTOREs and reads again, scoring the SUM, so a READ that always
returned the first item is still visible.
🟢 **`LSET`/`RSET` ARE EACH OTHER'S CONTROL.** Both read the FIRST byte of the
fielded buffer: left-justified it is the data, right-justified it is a pad space.
The same program with the other verb answers the other value, so neither row is
scoring merely "not a stub".

treated as a plain separator leaves 2), the SEMICOLON concatenates with no gap

it at all), and the exponential `^^^^` (`[ 1.23E+02]`; the exact spacing is not
predicted, what makes it a reading is that both machines produce the same one).

padding ONLY because its REMs are the LAST statement on their lines. The padding
is `A=n` now.

WORKS the program stops before printing, so a marker-anchored capture would read

MESSAGE, and the failing case holds `[0w1]` instead.
